quotes.text: Subscription schedules are available in both the Stripe Billing Dashboard and the API.
You can’t configure manual tax rates and enable automatic tax for the same phase
The invoice begins in a `draft` status and is finalized by Stripe
Setting a finite end date on the final phase in the Dashboard cancels the subscription at that date.
Creating the schedule doesn’t create proration invoice items during the migration.

You can only update the current and future phases on subscription schedules.

findings: The new complete guide still describes schedules that create a subscription or attach to an existing one, sequential phases (one active at a time), up to 10 current/future phases, phase transitions, and end_behavior (new 9-23, 110-112, 431-434). The old guide covered the same fundamentals (old 10-24, 111-113, 516-519). No completed live subscription or invoice payment was observed.

Old line 8 asserted classic Subscription editor only and a 30-day persisted editor choice; the November guide omits that restriction and expressly gives Dashboard create, edit, preview, cancel and use-case workflows (new 17, 35-43, 295-308, 361-425, 855-859). Release is documented through the API at new 833-840, not as a Dashboard action in this capture. Source 13 and concept 10/91 still state classic-only as current. Retain the May statement as dated historical UI guidance, remove its unqualified current claim, and do not infer every Dashboard account or interface variant has identical access.

The inheritance table gains default_settings.automatic_tax versus phases.automatic_tax as a fifth schedule/phase property, beyond the four in the May table and current source 36/concept 46 (new 118-137; old 119-133). New 139-141 adds consequential manual-tax exclusions and inheritance: set a phase's automatic_tax.enabled=false to use manual default_tax_rates, automatic tax and manual rates cannot both apply to the same phase, and retained manual rates are not a fallback after inherited automatic-tax calculation fails. These conditions deserve source and concept correction.

The first invoice draft and approximate one-hour finalization window is specifically for a schedule-created subscription with collection_method=charge_automatically and start_date=now in the illustrated case, with later open or paid depending on asynchronous outcome (new 231-237; old 223-229). Source 19 and concept 14 state the draft window for every schedule-created subscription, and contrast all direct subscription creation as immediate finalization. Narrow the schedule-side condition and retain the guide's qualified contrast; draft does not prove paid or settled.

The new use cases distinguish API end_behavior=release after a fixed duration from Dashboard Forever final phase; a finite Dashboard final end date cancels the subscription (new 522-526). Future start creates the subscription when the future date arrives (new 528-545), whereas backdating creates immediately and bills elapsed time while application controls access (new 555-573). Old 639-641 implied backdating itself allowed immediate website access; that is corrected. Source 57-58 and concept 68-69 should preserve timing and access separation.

The new from_subscription path creates one phase from the current billing period/configuration without proration invoice items during migration (new 582-594). Updating a schedule requires all current/future phases and settings to retain them; omitted parameters are unset, past phases remain response-only (new 310-320, 674-681; old 334-342). Source 46 and concept 77-82 should keep this destructive omission warning and avoid treating the single-item downgrade sample as a general template.

The new release section says pass the schedule ID, valid for not_started or active, remove remaining phases, preserve an existing subscription, and create no subscription when not_started (new 833-840). Cancellation is valid for not_started or active; if active with a subscription, it immediately cancels that subscription, while Dashboard deletion before start cancels the schedule before subscription creation (new 842-859). Source 18 and concept 16/84-87 collapse release/cancel into 'sub continues' or 'both canceled' without the not_started boundary; qualify these by schedule state.

Direct edits of listed subscription fields might automatically split an attached phase; new 455-511 retains the old warning and specifically says metadata edits do not propagate to the attached schedule. Source 50 and concept 56 make automatic split categorical; narrow to 'might' generally while retaining the concrete item-delete example at new 476-479. The new API examples predominantly use curl rather than old Node.js and include a Ruby downgrade example (new 249-275, 683-726); this sample-language change is presentational, not proof of SDK removal.
substantive_changes: New guide removes the old classic-editor-only statement and documents broader Dashboard paths, although account-specific UI availability is not proven (old 8; new 17, 295-425, 833-859).
New guide adds automatic_tax to schedule/phase inheritance and detailed manual-tax conflict, precedence and non-fallback rules (new 118-141 versus old 119-133).

New guide clarifies finite Dashboard final-phase cancellation versus API release, backdate access control, no proration items when attaching from_subscription, and not_started release/cancel effects (new 522-588, 833-859).

Most Node.js-to-curl example replacement and list-number/Markdown styling changes in the diff are presentational; the new Ruby downgrade example does not negate old Node.js sample behavior (new 683-726; old 781-823).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retain May 2026 classic-editor-only and 30-day persisted choice solely as dated old UI guidance, since the November guide gives Dashboard workflows without repeating that limitation (old 8; new 17, 295-425).

Retain established two-proration-setting scopes, phase metadata merge/unset behavior, 10 current/future phase limit, update-all-current/future destructive omission warning, and draft-invoice condition with exact qualifiers (old 50-80, 135-147, 223-229, 334-342; new 49-79, 143-155, 231-237, 310-320).

Retain May Node.js examples as dated examples rather than evidence of a required SDK or deprecated API; November examples use curl and a Ruby downgrade example (old 243-295, 781-823; new 249-275, 683-726).
conflicts: Source 13 and concept 10/91 say classic Dashboard editor only; old 8 said so, but new 17 and Dashboard sections omit it and describe workflows. Do not preserve the May UI restriction as a current universal limit.
Source 36 and concept 46 list exactly four inheritable schedule/phase attributes, while new 118-124 includes automatic_tax as a fifth with further tax rules at 135-141.

Source 19 and concept 14 generalize the initial draft invoice timing; new 235-237 conditions it on schedule-created charge_automatically and gives start_date=now as the example, with payment outcome asynchronous.
Source 50 and concept 56 say direct changes auto-split the active phase; new 466 says listed changes might create a new phase. The item-delete example at new 476 is specific.

Source 18 and concept 16/86-87 omit not_started release/cancel distinctions; new 833-859 says release before start creates no subscription, and Dashboard delete before start cancels the schedule before creation.
unresolved_questions: The November Dashboard instructions do not establish availability for every account, editor variant, or rollout; the removed classic-only sentence alone is not proof of a universal UI transition.
The capture documents possible invoice status after asynchronous finalization but no live invoice, payment success, settlement, or actual access grant.
The guide's Dashboard finite-end-date wording and API end_behavior=release are separate paths; no automatic equivalence should be inferred for unspecified Dashboard configurations.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/subscription-schedules, the November guide establishes that schedules create or attach to subscriptions, sequence phases, and update subscriptions as phases start (new 9-23, 45-47). It conditions the draft first invoice and approximate one-hour finalization on a schedule-created charge_automatically subscription, with later open or paid dependent on asynchronous payment outcome (new 231-237). It adds automatic_tax to the inheritable schedule/phase fields and warns that manual tax rates cannot coexist with automatic tax in one phase (new 118-141). [[source-stripe-subscriptions-schedules]] matches older core material but retains a May classic-editor-only limit and overstates the draft invoice, four-field inheritance and direct auto-split claims (source 13/19/36/50; old 8, 223-229, 551-561). Accounts v2 customer_account versus Customer v1 customer remain distinct, with preview qualification at new 241-275.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/subscription-schedules, substantive changes include Dashboard workflows without the May classic-only sentence, fifth automatic_tax inheritance with non-fallback tax rules, finite Dashboard end-date cancellation versus API release, backdate access control, and state-specific release/cancel consequences (new 17, 118-141, 522-588, 833-859; old 8, 119-133, 639-641, 958-974). [[source-stripe-subscriptions-schedules]] should date the May UI limit, qualify first-invoice draft timing at source 19, expand inheritance at 36, and change categorical auto-splitting at 50 to 'might' except the item-delete example. The old Node.js to new curl/Ruby sample change and Markdown numbering are presentation, not API deprecation (old 243-295; new 249-275). Schedule update omissions unset prior settings (new 318), release before start creates no subscription (new 835), and draft/open/paid invoice statuses do not establish actual payment or settlement.
